scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! Our department is OFF THE NETWORK -- every
single one of our machines, all at once, can't reach anything!! Something
around the box all our wires go into must be wrong, but I don't know what.
Could someone look at it and get us back on the network -- the whole
department is sitting here doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Routing control-plane on router2 (FRRouting/RIP configuration). The Layer-2 switch and hosts are fine; the issue is the dynamic routing not running on the router that aggregates the Internet Lab and Servers networks.

Mechanism: With RIP not configured on router2, it does not advertise 128.168.0.0/16 (lan_internet) or 1.0.0.0/8 (lan_servers) to router1, nor does it learn the campus 192.168.x/24 routes from router1. As a result, each subnet’s default gateway returns ICMP “Destination Net Unreachable” for off-LAN traffic, isolating the entire department.

Localization: router2, interfaces eth1 (to lan_internet 128.168.0.0/16), eth0 (to lan_servers 1.0.0.0/8), and eth2 (WAN to router1 on 20.0.0.0/8). Evidence: router2’s routing table shows only connected routes and no R (RIP) routes; its running config has no “router rip” stanza. Pings from campus to 128.168.0.2 fail with “From 192.168.3.1 Destination Net Unreachable” (router1 has no route to 128.168.0.0/16). Pings from 128.168.0.2 to campus fail with “From 128.168.0.1 Destination Net Unreachable” (router2 lacks 192.168.x/24 routes). Intra-LAN pings within 128.168.0.0/16 succeed, confirming L2 is healthy.

Root cause: RIP is not enabled/configured on router2, so no routes are exchanged with router1.

Corrective fix: On router2, enable RIP and advertise the correct networks:
- router rip
- version 2
- network 128.168.0.0/16
- network 1.0.0.0/8
- network 20.0.0.0/8
Then verify R routes appear on router1 and router2. Alternatively, add equivalent static routes. This will immediately restore reachability for the entire department.
